newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MIDWEEK CASH LUMBER REVIEW - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MIDWEEK CASH LUMBER REVIEW - AUG 13.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Carryover from last week's strong finish was minimal as trading slowed at the mill level through Tuesday, Random Lengths said in its midweek cash lumber update. A number of prices held or edged higher, though many offerings were subject to negotiation. Southern Pine prices softened.
In structural panels, strong order files supported firm to higher Fir and SYP plywood prices. Fill-in buying left OSB prices drifting, the lumber reporting agency said.
Canadian fee-free exports as of August 5 were 38.4 pct of quarterly July/Sept quota and 38.0 pct of April/March quota.

Western S-P-F prices carried some momentum over from last week's rally but mill sales eased. Wholesalers reported steady business, with some having difficulty covering specific fill-ins for customers. The #2&Btr 2x6 was easiest to sell. The 2x10 saw less competition from Hem-Fir. Std&Btr 2x4 edged up with quotes reaching $358. Stud mills struggled to book beyond one week.

Eastern S-P-F prices were firm on #1&2 items with 2x6 gaining $5 on strong demand. Mills boasted strong order files and wood available for prompt shipment drew premiums. The pipeline remained thinly supplied, causing some retailers to scramble to cover needs, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine producers lowered quotes and accepted counters to keep wood moving but found trading uninspired. A few mills still had order backlogs but several weeks of slow activity had eroded most producers' files. Prices of #2 slipped $8-13.
Inland dimension sales were better than average on Monday but slowed on Tuesday. A few pockets of softness cropped up.
Inland stud prices gained a bit but sales were sluggish. Prices of Ponderosa Pine 12-inch commons showed firming signs.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir prices were mostly flat to up. Producers said the market had a better tone and found it easier to get offers. Although the pace quieted from last week, there was some carryover. Demand was especially strong for Hem-Fir #2&Btr 2x12. Studs were flat, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine plywood sales showed good carryover from last week's faster pace. Mills contimued to focus more on building order files than pushing quotes, although prices rose on steady trading. Traders attributed the improved tone to anticipation of a September pickup.

Western plywood sheathing and underlayment prices edged higher in the wake of last week's fast finish. Order files that reached into late August and early September were a deterrent to mill sales Monday and Tuesday, and many buyers looked to the secondary market for faster shipments, the agency said.

OSB prices tended to drift down in spotty trading. Mills turned down block business at steeply discounted prices, while often taking $1-2 counters on singles. Most mills could ship next week but some quoted into the week of August 25. Western markets remained a relative strong point, with delivered prices holding or even rising in spots, Random Lengths said.
